label:
Lactotripeptide milk
(Ameal S, Evolus)
note: Two routes exist: this one ferments skimmed milk; the other digests casein with enzymes (patent US7785824). Trial evidence is mixed: a Cochrane review (Usinger 2012) found no confirmed ACE-inhibiting effect in people.

about.text: Milk soured with Lactobacillus helveticus, whose enzymes cut the casein so that two tiny peptides, Val-Pro-Pro (VPP) and Ile-Pro-Pro (IPP), come free. Both inhibit angiotensin-converting enzyme in the test tube, and the milk is sold in Japan and Finland to people with mild high blood pressure.

how.text: The bacterium's cell-wall proteinase cuts casein into a peptide of about 28 amino acids holding both sequences; the cell takes it up and its peptidases trim out VPP and IPP. Falling pH switches the proteinase off, and added amino acids lower the yield.

links.name: Patent EP1581062 (strain, 38-42 °C, times; Evolus = Valio; Calpis sour milk = L. helveticus + S. cerevisiae)

steps.note: Strains named are CNRZ 244 in the Dutch patent, CM4 in the Calpis work, and one isolated from Evolus.

processing.text: Skimmed milk or 9 % reconstituted skim milk powder; preferably 15-50 h. Calpis sour milk also holds Saccharomyces cerevisiae. A run reached pH 4.6 after 9-11 h, was held 5-7 h, then went to pH 4.0.
